title: Touring the Orpheum and Sullivan-Considine circuits with McCormick and Fitzgerald
summary: The trio of Leclerc, Guy McCormick and Dick Fitzgerald toured vaudeville about two years out of Chicago, including Kansas City. McCormick later opened the Little Club with Tony Donopolis.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: How far did you get out on the off-air circuit?

Well, we were two years, we played three or four circuits, Considine, Sullivan Considine, and we worked out of Chicago, you see. We went from here to Chicago and we had a fella handle our act, an agent, and he sent us from one place to another. We played Kansas City about four weeks in those days. Played Chicago, all the parks and everything like that. And, yeah.

Guy McCormick used to be one of the singers. He was an entertainer. He was an entertainer here for a year. He worked at the pub cap at the Tony Donopolis' place there. Used to be on... Not the Little Club.
Yeah, he opened up a Little Club with Tony Donopolis. When was that? Well, when he opened it up. That's naturally years and years ago. Was it before World War I or after?

It had to be after. After World War I or after. Yeah. Because that's when I started to play. I played in Little Club too. We played with Guy McCormick and myself. But when I was in the show business, I was with Guy McCormick, myself, and what's this other fellow's name, I can't even think of it now.
He's not from New Orleans, so it doesn't matter, huh?

No, no. He wasn't from New Orleans, he was from Chicago. Dick Fitzgerald, that's what he was. Dick Fitzgerald. Dick Fitzgerald. Yeah, we had a trio, you know. And we played quite a bit. We were about two years out on the road between the Sullivan Continent Circus and the Orphium. And there was another circuit in those days. I forget what it was. So, we...
